reason: Exhaustive probe (t16) over all 65504 finite FP16 inputs against a sound dual oracle (mpmath 120-bit sigmoid packed via struct.pack('<e') RNE, cross-checked against the artifact's own reference(), which agreed on all inputs) found 7 exact FP16 bit-pattern mismatches, all at near-zero inputs (|x|<=0.011) where the kernel's FP32 intermediate (libdevice.exp + div_rn) lands on the wrong side of an FP16 rounding midpoint — e.g. x=0.0029296875: exact sigmoid=0.500732421875-5.2e-10, just below the FP16 midpoint 0.500732421875, correct RNE=0x3801, kernel outputs 0x3802; symmetric negative-x cases likewise flipped. The contract (problem.txt, the operative contract here — no test.py/get_inputs narrowing the domain) requires each output to be the exact real sigmoid rounded ONCE to binary16 RNE, with exact bit patterns for every finite FP16 encoding, and states 'One failing legal input is evidence against the implementation'. These 7 inputs are legal, and this is an exact-rounding requirement, not a tolerance, so the double-rounding deviation is a defect, not an acceptable rounding/precision artifact. c2 and c3 (subnormal/underflow region concerns) are rebutted by the corrected negative-x region probe (t17: 1153 inputs, zero mismatches, underflow cutoff exactly matching the oracle). No unresolved claims remain; the Skeptic reviewed all evidence and recorded no new claims.
